text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian neuwspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Editorial says a bank decision to freeze capital of the country's main pyramid scheme VEFA Holding until May could trigger the company's collapse and lead to the unseating of President Sali Berisha's regime.

- Around 2,000 people in the northen town of Shkodra called on the government to resign, blaming it for the collapse of pyramid schemes. Some 40,000 Shkodra citizens are said to have deposited their savings into two pyramid schemes, Xhaferri and Populli.

- Opposition Democratic Alliance Party leader Neritan Ceka sent a strong protest letter to Voice of America radio, blaming its correspondent in Tirana for allegedly helping Albanian Intelligence Service (SHIK) to disperse protests in Tirana square.
- The collapse of pyramid schemes has affected young people as 70 percent of them were surviving from earnings in such companies.
- The newspaper says Berisha is trying to provoke tension in Kosovo in a bid to draw Albanians' attention from the pyramid scheme crisis.
- Parliament passed a law banning pyramid investment schemes and warned operators they could face a minimum of 20 years in jail and confiscation of their assets.
- The newspaper quotes sources within the ruling Democratic Party (DP) as saying some DP members have urged Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to quit.
- Thousands of Albanians took to the streets in Shkodra, Durres and Elbasan to protest against the pyramid investment schemes collapse, asking the government to give them money back.
- The main opposition Socialist Party (SP) has called for the government's dismissal. It says the government is responsible for the economic, social and political crisis in Albania.
- SP called on its supporters to stage a peaceful protest in Tirana against the government's failure to prevent pyramid schemes activity.
- Police authorities have said they will allow demonstrations against pyramid schemes on Sunday at Tirana football stadium, Vlora, Korca and Fushe Kruje.
